scope: Targeted patch to V1.10.57, not a full rewrite. Package version, app UI/persona, settings schema, key order, retry mechanics, scraping provider implementation, downloads/music/GitHub and unrelated code are preserved. Inference eligibility changes intentionally under the requested free-only rule.

changes.purpose: Automatically injected PDF/HTML/Markdown authoring skills; HTML execution/preflight guidance; larger document budget; format-aware continuation contract.
HTML/Markdown intent priority; bounded larger page targets/continuation; Markdown parsing; signed charts, area charts, source captions and strict chart validation.
Read-only scraping capability awareness; mandatory verified-zero-price AI gate across routing, pins, utility jobs, continuations and native plans; no paid tier probe; backend price ceilings.
Free-only checks on direct Gemini speech/transcription and EasyVoice synthesis; preserve read-only account/voice-list calls and existing device fallback.
Block potentially billed Stability inference before submission using the same free-only gate.
Cache identifier only: ensure the updated existing files arrive for offline use.
Guard queued/native inference with fresh free verification and zero-price caps; reject legacy paid plans.
Guard proactive/native inference with fresh free verification and zero-price caps; disable legacy unverified Groq fallback.
Mirror the native AI worker guard for the existing Android patch workflow.
Mirror the native proactive-ping guard for the existing Android patch workflow.

skills.pdf: Full-length documents; target detection up to 200 pages (targets are not guaranteed render counts); bounded continuation up to 40 parts, subject to existing app/model/time limits; explicit short requests preserved. Native chart types: bar/column/hbar/line/area/pie/donut. Themes, columns, stats, callouts and timeline syntax taught to Ember automatically.
skills.html: Higher-priority format-specific generation instructions, real inline-JS interactions, self-contained offline assets, responsive/accessibility/print rules, two preflight passes, CSP-aware sandbox guidance and no fake backend actions. Existing HTML executor and sandbox are unchanged.
skills.markdown: Portable CommonMark/GFM authoring instructions, truthful extension limitations, correct longer fences, escaped table pipes and Setext heading parsing.
skills.awareness: Runtime reads the existing EmberScraper state and provider labels without exposing keys or enabling settings. Supplied URLs use the existing scrape_url tool/preparation path; disabled tools, blocked sites and missing evidence are reported honestly.

free_only_policy.eligible_inference: Fresh catalog-verified zero-price OpenRouter text models with explicit text-only output metadata; existing anonymous/keyless routes are preserved without paid-account credentials.
free_only_policy.blocked_inference: Paid, unknown-price, stale, mixed-media and account-specific unverified API tiers. A :free name alone is not sufficient. Provider/model pins, Free Mode OFF, tool continuations, utility calls and native workers cannot bypass the gate. Non-OpenRouter keyed inference, including Groq/Gemini/Mistral/Cohere/Claude/Plugsky and paid cloud media/speech, is blocked rather than assuming a saved key is a non-billable free-tier key.
free_only_policy.price_enforcement: OpenRouter requests include provider.max_price prompt/completion/request/image ceilings of 0. Catalog proof expires after one hour. Native HTTP rejects redirects and legacy/unverified queued plans.
free_only_policy.preservation: No existing keys or provider pins are removed or rewritten by this patch. Unknown-tier providers remain listed/configured but cannot make inference calls. Existing explicit Free Mode preferences and strict-pin behavior are retained.
free_only_policy.failure: No verified free capacity means a visible error, not an upgrade or paid fallback. Existing provider quotas, availability, internet/CORS restrictions and enabled switches still apply.
free_only_policy.separate_scraping: The requested scraping API remains on its existing configuration and may consume its own provider quota. This patch does not promise all scraping is free or make every website accessible.
